title: Customs Amendment (Product Specific Rule Modernisation) Bill 2018
short_title: Customs Amendment (Product Specific Rule Modernisation) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would simplify how Australia gives domestic effect to product-specific origin rules under four trade agreements, affecting goods seeking preferential treatment for customs duty.
It would use direct references to treaty annexes instead of reproducing relevant rules in regulations, and align tariff classification references with the versions used by each agreement.
Commencement would be set by proclamation, with a six-month fallback after Royal Assent, while direct treaty references would preserve the existing rules’ operation.
changes: Australia could waive origin certificate requirements under specified agreements where that discretion is not yet implemented.
Singaporean retail sets could qualify where non-originating items account for no more than 10 per cent of the set’s customs value.
Singapore’s chemical origin rules would be applied directly through references to the treaty text.
summary.affected: Importers seeking preferential tariffs for goods covered by the relevant trade agreements are affected.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Customs Act to give effect to free trade agreement product specific rules by direct reference to annexes, replacing lengthy regulations, and includes updates for AANZFTA, ChAFTA, and JAEPA to meet a 1 January 2019 deadline, with AANZFTA trade totalling A$120 billion in 2017.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Customs Amendment (Product Specific Rule Modernisation) Bill 2018, which streamlines product-specific rules of origin for four free trade agreements (SAFTA, AANZFTA, JAEPA, ChAFTA) to allow updates without further legislative changes. The shadow minister also introduced the Fair Go for Australians in Trade Bill 2018, proposing measures to increase transparency, require independent national interest assessments, and ban clauses allowing foreign companies to sue the Australian government.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Broad
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment (Product Specific Rule Modernisation) Bill 2018 makes technical changes to four free trade agreements—with ASEAN-New Zealand, Japan, China and Singapore—to automatically update product-specific rules of origin in domestic law, repealing over 2,500 pages of regulations. The member for Mallee argued the bill must pass in 2018 to meet treaty commitments, and emphasised that trade fosters peace and understanding, citing Australia’s post-war trade relationship with Japan as an example.
